title: The maxExchangeRate headroom is not standardised, ranging from 2x to 4x with only one instance recording the price it is measured against
content:
Across the Morpho instances the ceiling varies without stated reason: 2 AUSD for Grove x Steakhouse AUSD V2 (A...7.4.4.1), 2 USDC for Grove x Steakhouse USDC V2 (A...3.1.7.2.2.4.3), 3 PYUSD for Sentora PYUSD V2 (A...7.5.4.1), 3 RLUSD for both Sentora RLUSD V2 and Grove x Steakhouse RLUSD V2 (A...7.6.4.1, A...7.7.4.1), and 4 PYUSD for Steakhouse PYUSD (A...3.1.7.3.2.4.3).

Only that last one records the baseline: "1 share can represent at most 4 PYUSD (**current share price is 2**)" — a 2x buffer. For every other instance the Artifact gives the ceiling but not the price, so the actual protection level is unknown from the document alone. A 3-unit ceiling is a 3x buffer on a fresh vault and a 1.05x buffer on one whose shares have reached 2.85, and those are very different controls.

Two readings compete and the text does not settle them. Either the multiple is calibrated per vault to something unstated — expected yield, strategy volatility, the manager's track record — or the ceilings are set ad hoc and the variation is drift rather than judgment. The absence of the baseline price is what makes the question unanswerable, and the presence of that price on exactly one instance shows the useful convention exists but is applied inconsistently.

The practical fix is small: record the share price observed at the time of setting, next to the ceiling, on every instance. That single field converts the parameter from an opaque number into an auditable ratio and would let a reviewer see at a glance which vaults are approaching their own limits.
description: Ceilings of 2, 3 and 4 units per share appear across comparable Morpho vaults, and only the Steakhouse PYUSD entry states the current share price
